subject: Physics
title: Units and Measurement
summary: Every physical quantity = number × unit. The SI system has 7 base units (m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd); every other unit is derived from them.

No measurement is perfect: least count limits precision, and errors (systematic, random, gross) limit accuracy. Errors combine by fixed rules — add absolute errors for sums, add relative errors for products, multiply by the power for powers.
Significant figures show how precise a number is. The answer of a calculation can never be more precise than the least precise input.

Dimensions express a quantity in terms of [M], [L], [T], [A], [K]… Dimensional analysis checks equations, converts units and derives relations — but it cannot find pure-number constants or handle sums of terms with different powers.

formulas.name: SI base quantities
formulas.formula: length m · mass kg · time s · current A · temperature K · amount mol · luminous intensity cd
formulas.mistake: Plane angle (rad) and solid angle (sr) are dimensionless, not base units.

formulas.name: Least count of vernier callipers
formulas.formula: LC = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = (value of 1 MSD)/(number of vernier divisions)

formulas.name: Vernier reading
formulas.mistake: Subtract a positive zero error, add a negative one — don't flip the sign.

formulas.name: Least count of screw gauge
formulas.formula: LC = pitch / (number of circular scale divisions)

formulas.name: Screw gauge reading
formulas.when: Diameter of a wire, thickness of a sheet.
formulas.mistake: Zero error is positive when the circular-scale zero lies below the reference line — check this before subtracting.

formulas.name: Mean value and absolute error
formulas.formula: a_mean = Σaᵢ/n;  Δaᵢ = |a_mean − aᵢ|;  Δa_mean = Σ|Δaᵢ|/n
formulas.mistake: Use the modulus of each deviation — never let errors cancel.

formulas.name: Errors in sum and difference
formulas.formula: Z = A ± B  ⇒  ΔZ = ΔA + ΔB
formulas.note: Errors always ADD, even when the quantities are subtracted.

formulas.name: Errors in product, quotient and power
formulas.formula: Z = Aᵖ Bᵠ / Cʳ  ⇒  ΔZ/Z = p(ΔA/A) + q(ΔB/B) + r(ΔC/C)
formulas.when: Formulas like g = 4π²L/T² or ρ = m/V.
formulas.note: Relative errors add for division too, and each is multiplied by its power.

formulas.name: Significant figure rules
formulas.formula: × and ÷: keep the least number of significant figures;  + and −: keep the least number of decimal places
formulas.mistake: Trailing zeros after a decimal point count; leading zeros never count.

formulas.name: Dimensional formula
formulas.formula: [Q] = [Mᵃ Lᵇ Tᶜ Aᵈ Kᵉ]; e.g. force [MLT⁻²], energy [ML²T⁻²], pressure [ML⁻¹T⁻²]

formulas.name: Principle of homogeneity
formulas.formula: Every term on both sides of a correct equation has the same dimensions
formulas.when: Checking whether an equation can be right.
formulas.mistake: A dimensionally correct equation can still be wrong by a pure number like ½ or 2π.

formulas.name: Unit conversion
formulas.formula: n₁[M₁ᵃ L₁ᵇ T₁ᶜ] = n₂[M₂ᵃ L₂ᵇ T₂ᶜ]  ⇒  n₂ = n₁ (M₁/M₂)ᵃ (L₁/L₂)ᵇ (T₁/T₂)ᶜ
formulas.when: Changing a value from SI to CGS (or any system).

examples.title: Vernier reading
examples.problem: A vernier has 10 divisions equal to 9 main-scale divisions of 1 mm. The main scale reads 2.0 cm and the 7th vernier division coincides. Reading? (no zero error)

examples.title: Screw gauge with zero error
examples.problem: Pitch 0.5 mm, 50 circular divisions. With jaws closed the zero is 4 divisions below the line. A wire gives MSR = 3.0 mm, CSR = 36. Diameter?

examples.title: Error in g from a pendulum
examples.problem: g = 4π²L/T². L has 2% error and T has 1% error. Maximum % error in g?

examples.title: Mean absolute error
examples.problem: Readings of a period: 2.63, 2.56, 2.42, 2.71, 2.80 s. Mean, mean absolute error and % error?
examples.solution: Mean = 2.62 s. Deviations: 0.01, 0.06, 0.20, 0.09, 0.18 → mean abs error = 0.11 s. % error = 4.1%.

examples.title: Converting G to CGS
examples.problem: G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². Value in dyne cm² g⁻²? ([G] = M⁻¹L³T⁻²)

examples.title: Significant figures in a product
examples.problem: Area of a rectangle 3.8 cm × 2.62 cm?
examples.solution: 3.8 × 2.62 = 9.956; 3.8 has 2 significant figures, so the answer is 10 cm² (written 1.0 × 10¹ cm²).

examples.title: Deriving the pendulum formula
examples.problem: Assume T depends on mass m, length l and g as T ∝ mᵃ lᵇ gᶜ. Find a, b, c.
examples.solution: [T] = [M]ᵃ[L]ᵇ[LT⁻²]ᶜ → M: a = 0; T: −2c = 1 → c = −½; L: b + c = 0 → b = ½. So T ∝ √(l/g) (the 2π comes from experiment).

topics.title: Base and derived units
topics.explain: Derived units come from base units: newton = kg m s⁻², joule = kg m² s⁻², pascal = kg m⁻¹ s⁻². Prefixes: nano 10⁻⁹, micro 10⁻⁶, milli 10⁻³, kilo 10³, mega 10⁶, giga 10⁹. Practical length units: 1 Å = 10⁻¹⁰ m, 1 fermi = 10⁻¹⁵ m, 1 light year ≈ 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m, 1 AU ≈ 1.5 × 10¹¹ m, 1 parsec ≈ 3.08 × 10¹⁶ m.

topics.title: Accuracy vs precision
topics.explain: Accuracy = how close to the true value. Precision = how close repeated readings are to each other (set by least count). A precise instrument can still be inaccurate if it has a zero error.

topics.title: Types of errors
topics.explain: Systematic errors (instrument zero error, imperfect method, personal bias) push all readings one way — reduce by better method and correction. Random errors vary unpredictably — reduce by taking more readings and averaging. Gross errors come from carelessness.

topics.title: Rounding off
topics.explain: Drop digits after the last significant one: if the next digit > 5 raise by one; < 5 leave it; = 5 make the last digit even (2.745 → 2.74, 2.735 → 2.74). Do the rounding only at the end of a calculation.

topics.title: Counting significant figures
topics.explain: All non-zero digits count. Zeros between non-zero digits count (2.005 → 4). Leading zeros never count (0.0024 → 2). Trailing zeros count only with a decimal point (2.400 → 4; 2400 is ambiguous — write 2.4 × 10³ for 2). Exact numbers (like 2 in 2πr) have infinite significant figures.

topics.title: Uses and limits of dimensional analysis
topics.explain: Uses: check an equation, convert units, derive a relation when the quantity depends on a product of powers. Limits: cannot find constants like ½ or 2π, fails for trigonometric/exponential/log relations, cannot handle a quantity that depends on a sum of terms, and cannot tell scalars from vectors.

topics.title: Dimensionless and same-dimension quantities
topics.explain: Strain, refractive index, angle, relative density are dimensionless. Same dimensions: work, energy, torque [ML²T⁻²]; impulse and momentum [MLT⁻¹]; stress, pressure, Young's modulus, energy density [ML⁻¹T⁻²]; frequency, angular velocity, velocity gradient [T⁻¹]; Planck's constant and angular momentum [ML²T⁻¹].

topics.title: Dimensions of common constants
topics.explain: Spring constant k and surface tension [MT⁻²]; thermal conductivity [MLT⁻³K⁻¹]; Boltzmann constant k_B [ML²T⁻²K⁻¹]; gas constant R [ML²T⁻²K⁻¹mol⁻¹]; specific heat [L²T⁻²K⁻¹]; viscosity η [ML⁻¹T⁻¹]; resistance, reactance and impedance [ML²T⁻³A⁻²]; capacitance [M⁻¹L⁻²T⁴A²]; inductance [ML²T⁻²A⁻²]; ε₀ [M⁻¹L⁻³T⁴A²]; μ₀ [MLT⁻²A⁻²]; magnetic field B [MT⁻²A⁻¹]. Derive any of them from a defining formula: k = F/x, K from Q/t = KAΔT/L, k_B = E/T, R = V/I.

topics.title: Experimental skills
topics.explain: Vernier callipers measure internal and external diameters and depth; the screw gauge measures wire diameter and sheet thickness with LC 0.01 mm. Always note zero error with jaws closed before measuring, take readings at several places and average.

ratta: 7 SI base units: m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd.
Vernier LC = MSD/N;  screw gauge LC = pitch/N.
Corrected reading = observed − zero error (sign included).
Sums: add absolute errors;  products/powers: add (power × relative error).
× ÷ → least significant figures;  + − → least decimal places.
Force MLT⁻², energy ML²T⁻², pressure ML⁻¹T⁻², h ML²T⁻¹, G M⁻¹L³T⁻².
Dimensional analysis can't give constants like 2π.
k (spring) MT⁻²;  thermal conductivity MLT⁻³K⁻¹;  k_B ML²T⁻²K⁻¹;  R, X_L, X_C ML²T⁻³A⁻².
